If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home instead of going camping in the desert.
My little brother is ill today, so my mother has to stay at home and ___ him.
Everyone trusts Faisal because he is very ___. He always tells the truth, even when it is difficult.

listen.script: Hi Omar, it's Khalid. I'm calling about football practice tomorrow. The coach phoned me this evening. Practice won't be at the school field at four o'clock as usual, because they're repairing the grass. We're meeting at the sports centre at five o'clock instead. Oh, and don't forget your water bottle. It's going to be really hot.
options: The school field is being repaired.
The weather will be too hot.

listen.script: Good morning, students. This is an announcement about the school library. This Thursday, the library will close early, at twelve o'clock, because the teachers have a meeting. If you need to return any books this week, please bring them before Thursday at twelve. The library will open again as normal on Sunday morning.
listen.q: What should students do if they have library books to return this week?
options: Return them before twelve o'clock on Thursday.
Give them to their teachers at the meeting.

read.passage: Last month, my class went on a school trip to AlUla. I was excited because I had seen photos of the old rocks and buildings, but I had never been there before. We travelled by bus, and the journey took a long time, so most of us slept on the way. When we arrived, our guide showed us Hegra, where people carved homes and tombs into the rocks more than two thousand years ago. I couldn't believe how big they were! In the evening, we ate dinner outside and looked at the stars. The sky was much clearer than in Riyadh. The only problem was that I forgot my jacket, and the desert gets very cold at night. Next time, I will pack more carefully.

qs.q: What did the writer know about AlUla before the trip?
options: What it looked like from photos
A lot, because they had visited it before

qs.q: What does the writer want to do differently next time?
options: Travel by car instead of bus

aloud: I've been studying English for three years, but I still find some words quite difficult to pronounce.
We were going to visit our grandparents last weekend, but the weather was terrible, so we stayed at home.

speak.prompt: Tell me about a special day you remember, for example a family celebration, a trip, or Eid. What happened, and why was it important to you?
speak.expect: The learner can give a simple, connected narrative of a past event in a linear sequence (first, then, after that), mainly using the past simple accurately with some past continuous or 'was going to'. They can describe feelings and give brief reasons and opinions ('It was special because...'). They use everyday vocabulary on familiar topics (family, food, travel, school) and are generally intelligible, with some L1 accent. They speak with noticeable pauses for planning and some self-correction, but keep going and can be understood. Errors with more complex structures occur but do not block meaning. Answers are typically several linked sentences, not just isolated phrases (as at A2), though they lack the precision, range and fluent elaboration expected at B2.
